transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-04-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: 38m
Attendees: Avery Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Rodriguez (Redwood SE), Sara Voss (RiftLane), Jared Ng (Platform Eng), Priya Menon (Product), Omar Aziz (BD), Ben Cho (Security)

[00:00] Avery (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick round robin and then we'll jump in. I'm Avery, AE on the partnerships team. Liam's our SE.
[00:12] Sara (RiftLane): Hi all, Sara here. Excited to talk through how we might list Redwood as a managed inference option in the RiftLane marketplace.
[00:20] Liam (Redwood SE): Hey, happy to be here. We'll mostly cover architecture options and what a minimal POC looks like.
[00:28] Priya (Product): Quick context - RiftLane runs a marketplace for GPU compute where third parties can list software or managed services. Our goals: reduce integration friction for partners, keep billing simple, and ensure security posture for enterprise buyers.
[00:42] Omar (BD): Also exploring go-to-market alignment and revenue splits.
[00:46] Avery: Great. High level: there are two common patterns we've done — 1) forwarding/proxy model where RiftLane calls Redwood's hosted API and handles billing, and 2) a native connector where Redwood runs a co-located runtime on RiftLane GPU instances (private deployment). Each has tradeoffs.
[01:05] Jared (Platform): Can you expand on the native option? That sounds like on-premish or VPC style?
[01:10] Liam: Yeah, we call it Redwood Private in our docs. It's basically a customer-hosted control plane and runtime that can be deployed into a VPC or on prem. For a marketplace that would be our 'co-locate' model — you run the inference runtime on your nodes and we provide an agent + SDK for billing and metrics. There's also a lighter-weight connector where you just forward API calls to Redwood Hosted and we return responses; in that case you don't manage GPUs.
[01:33] Ben (Security): For the co-locate model, how do we do key management? We need to know whether Redwood stores customer keys or if we use our KMS.
[01:40] Liam: Good question. We support both. For Private we can integrate with your KMS/HSM — keys never leave your environment. For Hosted we do full encryption in transit and at rest and we can offer bring-your-own-key flows. I'll share the KMS section in the security pack.
[01:56] Sara: From a marketplace perspective, the simplest launch would be the forwarding model so we can get a listing quickly, but long term we prefer a co-located option for enterprise buyers who want data residency and lower unit costs.
[02:08] Avery: Totally makes sense. Pilot usually starts with forwarding to validate demand and UX, then we scope a co-locate pilot. Typical timeline: 2–4 week feature trial + 1–2 week benchmark run.
[02:20] Priya: What about billing? We need per-minute/per-token metering that maps to our billing platform.
[02:27] Liam: We emit usage events and webhooks; there's also an invoicing API. For marketplace integration we can send granular token/embedding usage events so you can bill end customers precisely. There's some mapping work — for example, batching can blur per-request token counts — but we provide guidance on attribution.
[02:45] Jared: That batching comment is important — some of our customers care about latency, others care about price. Does Redwood expose batching controls per customer or per route?
[02:54] Liam: Yes, you can configure batching policies per route/model. You can also set max-wait thresholds to preserve SLOs. In practice we do continuous batching but you can pin low-latency policies for certain tenants.
[03:06] Sara: Good. Let's talk security checklist — SOC2, audit logs, RBAC?
[03:11] Avery: Short answer: we are SOC 2 compliant, provide audit logs, have RBAC and SSO/SAML integrations, and support customer-managed keys for Private. Ben, if you send a list we'll map answers.
[03:22] Ben: I'll put the list together. Also curious about data retention and purge controls for debug logs.
[03:27] Liam: We have retention settings and can purge logs on request; for Private deployments those logs can be kept only in your control plane.
[03:34] Priya: On the product side, what metrics would we surface in the listing? Latency percentiles and cost per token are what buyers usually look for.
[03:41] Avery: We can provide performance profiles per model — p50/p95 latency at sequence lengths, estimated tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens for different quantization profiles. We also publish recommended model variants for cost/latency tradeoffs.
[03:55] Omar: Revenue share — is that something Redwood has precedent on?
[03:59] Avery: We generally do revenue share for marketplace partners, but terms are negotiable — could be percentage of net usage, or a flat fee plus split. We'll propose a standard partner addendum to start.
[04:12] Jared: Curious about POC hardware — what GPUs should we provision? We have mixed fleet: A100 40GB, A800s, and some back-office T4s.
[04:21] Liam: For a realistic production test I'd recommend A800 for cost parity with cloud and A100 if you want to test large-context models. We'll include quantized runs to estimate cost. For throughput tests we care about batch sizes and typical prompt lengths.
[04:35] Sara: Are there any known gotchas when running on A800 vs A100?
[04:39] Liam: Driver and CUDA versions matter; also kernel selection can differ slightly. Our runtime auto-selects kernels but we need SSH/agent access during benchmark to tune settings. Sometimes the K-V cache memory behavior shows up differently on smaller VRAM nodes — we call it K-V cache but transcripts show it as K V cash — ha.
[04:57] Priya: (laughing) noted.
[05:00] [00:05:00] Avery: Let's sketch a minimal POC scope: 1) Forwarding listing with sample UI/marketing copy, 2) 48-hour benchmark using RiftLane staging GPUs measuring p50/p95 latency and tokens/sec across 3 model families, 3) security questionnaire answered. Success criteria: p95 < 600ms on small generation use case or agreed SLA, and acceptable cost per 1k tokens.
[05:25] Jared: How do you handle failover — if Redwood hosted is down, can we route to a fallback model or do we show outage?
[05:31] Liam: We have smart routing and fallback policies: you can configure region fallback, model variant fallback (smaller quantized model), or show a degrade mode. For marketplace UX you'd likely want a message plus an option to queue requests.
[05:44] Sara: From ops side, we need a simple on-boarding flow for merchants — self-serve or manual?
[05:49] Avery: We support both. For high-volume merchants we recommend a short onboarding with an AE and SE. For smaller plugins you can do a self-serve API key flow. We'll share templates for both.
[05:58] Priya: I want to understand the data flow. If we do forwarding: customer -> RiftLane gateway -> Redwood hosted. Do you send back structured telemetry for billing?
[06:07] Liam: Yes, webhook events with request_id, tokens_in/tokens_out, model_id, and latencies. We also provide traces you can hook into via headers for debugging.
[06:15] Ben: About compliance: do you have a BAA or any healthcare-specific docs?
[06:20] Avery: We have a standard security pack and we've signed BAAs before — Ben, we'll route the relevant docs. For high compliance we typically recommend Private deployment.
[06:29] [00:07:00] Jared: One integration detail — can we surface per-merchant keys so each merchant's usage maps to their ledger in our billing system?
[06:36] Liam: Absolutely. We can mint per-tenant API keys or issue scoped tokens so usage attribution is precise.
[06:42] Sara: For marketplace listing content, can we include templates — model descriptions, recommended prompts, and benchmark numbers?
[06:49] Avery: We'll provide a one-pager with suggested copy, recommended prompts, and performance stats.
[06:55] Omar: For go-to-market, we might want joint PR and a launch discount during the first quarter. Is Redwood open to promo credits?
[07:02] Avery: Yes, we do partner promos and early credits — we can include that in the partner playbook.
[07:07] [00:08:00] Priya: Let's talk quotas and rate limits. Our marketplace needs to enforce per-merchant quotas. Does Redwood allow configurable rate limits per key?
[07:14] Liam: Yes, per-key quotas and rate limiting are supported. You can also set soft/burst limits.
[07:19] Ben: Auditability on those events is critical — we need immutable logs for 12 months. Can Redwood export to our SIEM?
[07:27] Liam: We can stream logs to your S3 or syslog/ELK. For hosted we also retain logs per contract; for Private you control retention.
[07:35] Sara: Ok, sounds promising. Any blockers from your side on revenue share or technical model?
[07:40] Avery: Not from Redwood — mostly need access to your staging fleet and an agreed set of prompts for benchmarks. Also need Ben's security questionnaire answered.
[07:49] Jared: We'll provision a 6-node A800 pool in staging and share credentials with a scoped user for the duration.
[07:55] [00:09:00] Liam: Perfect. For the benchmark we'll run three families: a small Llama-style quantized model, a mid-sized instruction model, and a larger LLM to surface tail latencies. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens across quantized vs fp16.
[08:15] Priya: Can you give a ballpark for cost delta between Hosted vs Private-on-RiftLane?
[08:20] Liam: It depends on utilization. For low utilization Hosted can be cheaper. If you have steady utilization and can pack instances, co-locate/Private is usually 20–40% cheaper at scale due to avoidance of per-request handling and better batching. Quantization also reduces cost. We'll include model-specific numbers in the proposal.
[08:37] Omar: Any legal constraints for marketplace? We need indemnity language and terms for shared customers.
[08:42] Avery: Our legal team has a marketplace addendum template; we'll share, but final terms depend on deal size.
[08:49] [00:10:00] Sara: Quick question — do you support function-calling/tool-calls from within the models? Some of our customers expect that.
[08:55] Liam: Yes, we support function/tool calling and structured output. That works in Hosted and Private, though for Private you might need to hook to local services for secure tool calls.
[09:05] Ben: About SSO — can we map roles and have tenant-scoped RBAC?
[09:10] Liam: Yes, SAML/SSO with SCIM provisioning and tenant-scoped roles are supported.
[09:15] Priya: For the product page listing, what would be the differentiator text? Latency, reliability, and easy onboarding?
[09:21] Avery: I'd pitch it as "Redwood inference — production-ready, cost-optimized LLM inference with on-demand or co-located deployment options." We'll give you a short blurb and a longer tech spec.
[09:33] [00:11:00] Jared: For the benchmarking test, will Redwood run client-side load or do we run locally from RiftLane?
[09:39] Liam: Usually we run the driver from within the staging VPC to avoid cross-region noise. We'll coordinate to use a RiftLane runner to generate realistic traffic patterns.
[09:48] Omar: On commercial splits, we might want a tiered split — higher for enterprise customers.
[09:53] Avery: That's typically doable; we'll surface a few templates.
[09:58] Priya: Anything else from security?
[10:01] Ben: Just the BAA and a CLA on data handling; I'll compile a list.
[10:06] [00:12:00] Sara: Are there any partner portals or partner APIs Redwood exposes for listing management?
[10:12] Avery: We have a partner API for provisioning listings, webhook subscription, and usage reports — we can give sandbox credentials for the POC.
[10:20] Priya: Good. On product terms, can we co-brand the console view? Some merchants like to see their provider in the UI.
[10:27] Avery: Co-branding is possible for marketplace partners. We'll include that in the playbook.
[10:31] [00:13:00] Liam: Small note about latency tuning — if you plan to run multi-tenant workloads on a single node, prefix caching is key. We have KV cache warmers to speed up repeated prompts, but that requires warm-up traffic patterns.
[10:45] Jared: We'll design the runner to warm caches.
[10:48] Priya: For our merchants that need low-cost embeddings, does Redwood expose an embeddings-only endpoint?
[10:52] Liam: Yes, embeddings endpoints exist and can be priced differently; you can also cache embeddings at the marketplace layer.
[10:58] [00:14:00] Sara: OK let's put some dates on this — can we aim to have a benchmark run by 2027-04-22?
[11:04] Avery: That's tight but possible if staging is provisioned by 2027-04-19 and we get prompts and keys. Otherwise the week after is safer.
[11:10] Jared: We'll try to have staging ready by the 19th.
[11:13] Omar: I'll coordinate GTM and marketing collateral.
[11:15] [00:15:00] Avery: Great. I'm going to summarize actions: I'll send integration spec, security pack and partner playbook; Liam will share benchmark plan; Jared will provision staging; Ben will send security questions; Priya/Omar will review partner terms.
[11:35] Priya: Sounds good. A few clarifying questions before we wrap: do you have sample UI components for the listing card and a sample contract?
[11:42] Avery: Yes — sample listing card, suggested copy, and the partner addendum will go in the email.
[11:46] Ben: One last thing on logs: we need an SLA on ingestion and export for audit logs.
[11:51] Liam: We'll include log export latency in the security doc. For hosted it's typically under 5 minutes to S3.
[11:58] [00:16:00] Sara: Great, that covers most things. Any final questions?
[12:02] [crosstalk] Omar: No, just excited to move forward.
[12:06] Avery: Thanks everyone — we'll send the packet and propose a follow-up for week of 2027-04-26 for a technical deep dive.
[12:15] Priya: Works for me.
[12:18] Jared: Thanks, bye.
[12:20] [00:16:30] End of transcript (auto-generated). Note: transcription has minor errors — some product names and acronyms may be slightly off.
